questions.q: During the electrolysis of acidified water, 16 g of O$_2$ gas is formed at anode. The volume of H$_2$ gas liberated at cathode under STP conditions is
questions.explanation: 0.5 mol O$_2$ (16 g) requires 4$\times$0.5 = 2 mol electrons (O$_2$ formation needs 4 e$^-$); these 2 mol electrons liberate 2/2 = 1 mol H$_2$ (2 e$^-$ per H$_2$), i.e. 22.4 L at STP.

questions.q: $\Lambda_m^o(NH_4OH)$ is equal to
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law, the limiting molar conductivity of the weak electrolyte NH$_4$OH can be obtained from those of strong electrolytes: $\Lambda_m^o(NH_4Cl) + \Lambda_m^o(NaOH) - \Lambda_m^o(NaCl)$.

questions.q:
Given below are the half-cell reactions:
Mn$^{2+}$ + 2e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Mn (E$^\circ$ = -1.18 V)
Mn$^{3+}$ + e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Mn$^{2+}$ (E$^\circ$ = +1.51 V)
The E$^\circ_{cell}$ for 3Mn$^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ Mn + 2Mn$^{3+}$ will be ______
options: - 2.69 V, the reaction will not occur (Non-Spontaneous)
- 0.33 V, the reaction will not occur (Non-Spontaneous)
questions.explanation: E$^\circ_{cell}$ = E$^\circ_{cathode}$ - E$^\circ_{anode}$ = (-1.18) - (+1.51) = -2.69 V; a negative E$^\circ_{cell}$ means the disproportionation is non-spontaneous.

questions.q: The conductivity of centimolar solution of KCl at 298 K is 0.021 Ohm$^{-1}$ cm$^{-1}$ and the resistance of the cell containing the solution at 298 K is 60 $\Omega$. The value of cell constant (G*) is
questions.explanation: Cell constant $G^* = \kappa \times R = 0.021 \times 60 = 1.26$ cm$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The correct statement/s about Galvanic cell is/are (a) Current flows from cathode to anode (b) Anode is positive terminal (c) If E$_{cell}$ < 0, then it is spontaneous reaction (d) Cathode is positive terminal
questions.explanation: In a galvanic cell the cathode is the positive terminal and conventional current flows externally from the cathode (+) to the anode (-); the anode is negative (not positive), and a reaction is spontaneous only when E$_{cell}$ > 0, so statements (a) and (d) are correct.

questions.q: The electronic conductance depends on
options: The number of valence electrons per atom
questions.explanation: Electronic conductance (in metals) arises from the movement of valence electrons, so it depends on the number of valence electrons per atom; the other options affect ionic conductance instead.

questions.q: For a given half cell, Al$^{3+}$ + 3e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Al on increasing the concentration of aluminium ion, the electrode potential will
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation, $E = E^\circ - \dfrac{RT}{3F}\ln\dfrac{1}{[Al^{3+}]}$, so increasing [Al$^{3+}$] increases the electrode potential.

questions.q: Match the following and select the correct option for the quantity of electricity, in Cmol$^{-1}$, required to deposit various metals at cathode. List-I: (a) Ag$^+$ (b) Mg$^{2+}$ (c) Al$^{3+}$ (d) Ti$^{4+}$; List-II: (i) 386000 Cmol$^{-1}$ (ii) 289500 Cmol$^{-1}$ (iii) 96500 Cmol$^{-1}$ (iv) 193000 Cmol$^{-1}$
options: a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
a - iii, b - iv, c - ii, d - i
a - iv, b - iii, c - i, d - ii
questions.explanation: The charge needed equals n times the Faraday constant (96500 C): Ag$^+$ needs 1F=96500 (iii), Mg$^{2+}$ needs 2F=193000 (iv), Al$^{3+}$ needs 3F=289500 (ii), Ti$^{4+}$ needs 4F=386000 (i).

questions.q: How many Coulombs are required to oxidise 0.1 mole of H$_2$O to oxygen?
questions.explanation: H$_2$O $\rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}$O$_2$ + 2H$^+$ + 2e$^-$ needs 2 Faradays per mole; for 0.1 mol, charge = 0.1 $\times$ 2 $\times$ 96500 = $1.93\times10^4$ C.

questions.q: A current of 3A is passed through a molten calcium salt for 1 hr 47 min 13 sec. The mass of calcium deposited is: (Molar mass of Ca = 40 g mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: Time = 6433 s; charge = 3 $\times$ 6433 = 19299 C $\approx$ 0.2 mol electrons; since Ca$^{2+}$ + 2e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Ca, moles of Ca = 0.1, mass = 0.1 $\times$ 40 = 4.0 g.

questions.q: The value of 'A' in the equation $\lambda_m = \lambda_m^0 - A\sqrt{C}$ is the same for the pair
questions.explanation: The Kohlrausch constant 'A' depends on the charge (valence) type of the electrolyte; NaCl and KBr are both 1:1 electrolytes and so share the same 'A'.

questions.q: The resistance of 0.1 M weak acid HA in a conductivity cell is 2 $\times$ 10$^3$ Ohm. The cell constant of the cell is 0.78 cm$^{-1}$ and $\lambda^\circ_m$ of acid HA is 390 S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$. The pH of the solution is
questions.explanation: $\kappa = \dfrac{\text{cell constant}}{R} = \dfrac{0.78}{2000} = 3.9\times10^{-4}\,S/cm$; $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa\times1000}{0.1} = 3.9\,S\,cm^2mol^{-1}$; $\alpha = \Lambda_m/\lambda^\circ_m = 0.01$; $[H^+]=c\alpha=10^{-3}\,M \Rightarrow pH = 3$.

questions.q: During the electrolysis of brine, by using inert electrodes,
questions.explanation: Due to overvoltage effects, Cl$^-$ is preferentially discharged over water at the anode giving Cl$_2$ gas, while water is preferentially reduced at the cathode giving H$_2$ gas rather than Na metal.

questions.q: Consider the following 4 electrodes: A : Ag$^+$ (0.0001 M)/Ag$_{(s)}$; B : Ag$^+$ (0.1 M) / Ag$_{(s)}$; C : Ag$^+$ (0.01 M)/Ag$_{(s)}$; D : Ag$^+$ (0.001 M) / Ag$_{(s)}$; E$^\circ_{Ag^+/Ag}$ = +0.80 V. Then reduction potential in volts of the electrodes in the order
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation $E=E^\circ+0.0591\log[Ag^+]$, reduction potential increases with $[Ag^+]$; since B(0.1 M) > C(0.01 M) > D(0.001 M) > A(0.0001 M) in concentration, the reduction potentials follow the same order.

questions.q: In Fuel cells _____ are used as catalysts.
questions.explanation: In H$_2$-O$_2$ fuel cells, finely divided platinum and palladium are commonly used as electrode catalysts.

questions.q: The molar conductivity is maximum for the solution of concentration
questions.explanation: Molar conductivity increases as concentration decreases; of the given values, 0.001 M is the lowest concentration, so it gives the maximum molar conductivity.

questions.q: Specific conductance of 0.1 M HNO$_3$ is 6.3 $\times$ 10$^{-2}$ ohm$^{-1}$ cm$^{-1}$. The molar conductance of the solution is
questions.note: The standard answer should be (B) 630 ohm$^{-1}$ cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, since $\Lambda_m=\kappa\times1000/M$ gives 630, not 6.300; option (A) appears to be a printing/decimal-placement error in the key.
questions.explanation: $\Lambda_m$ = $\kappa$ $\times$ 1000/M = (6.3 $\times$ 10$^{-2}$ $\times$ 1000)/0.1 = 630 ohm$^{-1}$ cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, which matches option (B); the KEA key, however, marks option (A) 6.300 as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: For spontaneity of a cell, which is correct?
questions.explanation: A cell reaction is spontaneous only when its Gibbs free energy change is negative ($\Delta$G = -ve), which also corresponds to a positive cell potential.

questions.q: Consider the following electrodes: P = Zn$^{2+}$ (0.0001 M)/Zn, Q = Zn$^{2+}$ (0.1 M)/Zn, R = Zn$^{2+}$ (0.01 M)/Zn, S = Zn$^{2+}$ (0.001 M)/Zn. E$^\circ$Zn/Zn$^{2+}$ = − 0.76 V. Electrode potentials of the above electrodes in volts are in the order
questions.explanation: By Nernst equation, E = E° + (0.0592/2)log[Zn$^{2+}$], so electrode potential increases with concentration: Q(0.1M) > R(0.01M) > S(0.001M) > P(0.0001M).

questions.q: The resistance of 0.01 m KCl solution at 298 K is 1500 Ω. If the conductivity of 0.01 m KCl solution at 298 K is 0.146 × 10$^{-3}$ S cm$^{-1}$. The cell constant of the conductivity cell in cm$^{-1}$ is
questions.explanation: Cell constant = conductivity × resistance = 0.146×10$^{-3}$ × 1500 = 0.219 cm$^{-1}$.

questions.q: H$_{2(g)}$ + 2AgCl$_{(s)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2 Ag$_{(s)}$ + 2HCl$_{(aq)}$. E$^\circ_{cell}$ at 25°C for the cell is 0.22 V. The equilibrium constant at 25°C is
The pair of electrolytes that possess the same value for the constant (A) in the Debye-Huckel-Onsagar equation, $\lambda_m = \lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt C$ is
questions.explanation: The constant A depends only on the charge type (valence factor) of the electrolyte; NH$_4$Cl and NaBr are both 1:1 electrolytes and so share the same A, unlike the other mixed-valence pairs.

questions.q: Given: E$^\circ_{Fe^{+3}/Fe^{+2}}$ = +0.76 V and E$^\circ_{I_2/I^-}$ = +0.55 V. The equilibrium constant for the reaction taking place in the galvanic cell consisting of the above two electrodes is $\left[\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.06\right]$
If an aqueous solution of NaF is electrolyzed between inert electrodes, the product obtained at anode is
questions.explanation: F$^-$ is very difficult to oxidise (very high oxidation potential required), so water is preferentially oxidised at the anode to give O$_2$.

questions.q: One litre solution of MgCl$_2$ is electrolyzed completely by passing a current of 1A for 16 min 5 sec. The original concentration of MgCl$_2$ solution was (Atomic mass of Mg = 24)
questions.explanation: Charge passed = 1A $\times$ 965 s = 965 C, i.e. 965/96500 = 0.01 mol electrons; since Mg2+ + 2e- $\rightarrow$ Mg, moles Mg (=moles MgCl2) completely deposited = 0.01/2 = 0.005 mol in 1 L, giving $5\times10^{-3}$ M.

questions.q: An aqueous solution of CuSO$_4$ is subjected to electrolysis using inert electrodes. The pH of the solution will
options: increase or decrease depending on the strength of the current.
questions.explanation: At the anode, water is oxidised to O2 releasing H+ ions (SO4^2- is not oxidised preferentially), while Cu2+ is reduced at the cathode; the accumulation of H+ makes the solution more acidic, so pH decreases.

questions.q: Given: E$^\circ_{Mn^{+7}/Mn^{+2}}$ = 1.5 V and E$^\circ_{Mn^{+4}/Mn^{+2}}$ = 1.2 V, then E$^\circ_{Mn^{+7}/Mn^{+4}}$ is
questions.explanation: Using $\Delta G$ additivity: $5(1.5) = 2(1.2) + 3E^\circ_{Mn^{+7}/Mn^{+4}}$, so $7.5-2.4=3E^\circ$, giving $E^\circ=1.7$ V.

questions.q: The charge required for the reduction of 1 mole of MnO$_4^-$ to MnO$_2$ is
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 in MnO$_4^-$ to +4 in MnO$_2$, a gain of 3 electrons per mole, requiring 3 Faradays of charge.

questions.q: At a particular temperature, the ratio of molar conductance to specific conductance of 0.01 M NaCl solution is
questions.explanation: $\Lambda_m/\kappa$ = 1000/C (with C in mol/L); for C = 0.01 M, this ratio = 1000/0.01 = 10$^5$ cm$^3$ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.q: For a cell reaction involving two electron changes, E$^0_{cell}$ = 0.3 V at 25$^\circ$C. The equilibrium constant of the reaction is

The standard reduction potential at 298 K for the following half cell reactions

Zn$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ + 2e $\rightarrow$ Zn$_{(s)}$  E$^\circ$ = – 0.762 V

Cr$^{3+}_{(aq)}$ + 3e $\rightarrow$ Cr$_{(s)}$  E$^\circ$ = 0.740 V

2H$^+_{(aq)}$ + 2e $\rightarrow$ H$_{2(g)}$  E$^\circ$ = 0.0 V

F$_{2(g)}$ + 2e $\rightarrow$ 2F$^-_{(aq)}$  E$^\circ$ = 2.87 V

Which of the following is strongest reducing agent ?
questions.explanation: The species with the most negative standard reduction potential is oxidised most easily; Zn (E$^\circ$=–0.762 V) is therefore the strongest reducing agent among those listed.

questions.q:
By passing electric current, NaClO$_3$ is converted into NaClO$_4$ according to the following equation

NaClO$_3$ + H$_2$O $\rightarrow$ NaClO$_4$ + H$_2$

How many moles of NaClO$_4$ will be formed when three Faradays of charge is passed through NaClO$_3$ ?
questions.explanation: Converting ClO$_3^-$ to ClO$_4^-$ involves loss of 2 electrons per ion (Cl: +5 → +7); 3 F ÷ 2 F/mol = 1.5 mol of NaClO$_4$.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride solution, which of the half cell reaction will occur at anode ?
questions.explanation: Despite the lower theoretical oxidation potential requirement for water, Cl$^-$ is preferentially oxidised at the anode due to overpotential effects, releasing Cl$_2$ gas — the basis of the chlor-alkali process.

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect in a galvanic cell ?
options: The electrode at which electrons are gained is called cathode.
The electrode at which electrons are lost is called cathode.
questions.explanation: The electrode where electrons are lost (oxidation) is the anode, not the cathode; statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.q: A secondary cell is one
options: can be recharged by passing current through it in the same direction.
can be recharged by passing current through it in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: A secondary (rechargeable) cell is recharged by passing current through it in the direction opposite to the discharge current.

questions.q: The amount of current in Faraday is required for the reduction of 1 mol of Cr$_2$O$_7^{--}$ ions to Cr$^{3+}$ is,
questions.explanation: Each Cr goes from +6 to +3, gaining 3 electrons; with 2 Cr atoms per Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$, total electrons gained = 6, so 6 F is required.

questions.q: While charging the lead storage battery, ________.
options: PbSO$_4$ on anode is reduced to Pb
PbSO$_4$ on cathode is reduced to Pb
PbSO$_4$ on cathode is oxidized to Pb
PbSO$_4$ on anode is oxidized to PbO$_2$
questions.explanation: The Pb plate is conventionally called the anode and the PbO$_2$ plate the cathode; on recharging (electrolysis) the reactions reverse, so PbSO$_4$ on the anode (Pb plate) is reduced back to Pb.

questions.q: In H$_2$ – O$_2$ fuel cell the reaction occurring at cathode is
questions.explanation: In an alkaline H$_2$-O$_2$ fuel cell, reduction of oxygen occurs at the cathode: O$_2$ + 2H$_2$O + 4e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ 4OH$^-$.

questions.q: How many Coulombs of electricity are required for the oxidation of one mol of water to dioxygen?
questions.explanation: 2H$_2$O $\rightarrow$ O$_2$ + 4H$^+$ + 4e$^-$ transfers 4 mol electrons per 2 mol water, i.e. 2 mol electrons per mol water; charge = 2 $\times$ 96500 C = 1.93 $\times$ 10$^5$ C.

questions.q:
Conductivity of a saturated solution of a sparingly soluble salt AB at 298 K is 1.85 × 10$^{-5}$ S m$^{-1}$. Solubility product of the salt AB at 298 K is

Given $\Lambda^\circ_m$(AB) = 140 × 10$^{-4}$ S m$^2$ mol$^{-1}$

For Cr$_2$O$_7^{-2}$ + 14H$^+$ + 6e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ 2Cr$^{+3}$ + 7H$_2$O; E° = 1.33 V At [Cr$_2$O$_7^{-2}$] = 4.5 millimole, [Cr$^{+3}$] = 15 millimole, E is 1.067 V. The pH of the solution is nearly equal to
questions.explanation: Using the Nernst equation E = E° - (0.059/6)log([Cr$^{3+}$]$^2$/([Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$][H$^+$]$^{14}$)), solving for [H$^+$] with the given concentrations and potentials gives a pH close to 2.

questions.q:
Impure copper containing Fe, Au, Ag as impurities is electrolytically refined. A current of 140 A for 482.5 s decreased the mass of the anode by 22.26 g and increased the mass of cathode by 22.011 g. Percentage of iron in impure copper is

(Given molar mass Fe = 55.5 g mol$^{-1}$, molar mass Cu = 63.54 g mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: Total charge = 140×482.5 = 67550 C; charge used to deposit 22.011 g Cu at the cathode = (22.011/63.54)×2×96500 ≈ 66863 C; remaining charge (≈687 C) dissolved Fe from the anode, giving mass Fe ≈ 0.198 g, so %Fe = 0.198/22.26×100 ≈ 0.90%. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q:
For hydrogen – oxygen fuel cell at one atm and 298 K

H$_{2(g)}$ + $\dfrac{1}{2}$O$_{2(g)}$ $\longrightarrow$ H$_2$O$_{(l)}$; ΔG° = –240 kJ

E° for the cell is approximately,

(Given F = 96,500 C)
The emf of a galvanic cell constituted with the electrodes Zn$^{2+}$ | Zn (- 0.76 V) and Fe$^{2+}$| Fe(-0.41 V) is
questions.explanation: Fe has the higher reduction potential so it is the cathode; EMF = E(cathode) - E(anode) = -0.41 - (-0.76) = +0.35 V.

questions.q: The approximate time duration in hours to electroplate 30 g of calcium from molten calcium chloride using a current of 5 amp is [At. mass of Ca = 40]
questions.explanation: Moles of Ca $=30/40=0.75$; charge needed $=0.75\times2\times96500=144750$ C; time $=144750/5=28950$ s $\approx 8$ hours.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant of the reaction: A$_{(s)}$ + 2B$^+_{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons$ A$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ + 2B$_{(s)}$; E°$_{cell}$ = 0.0295 V is [$\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.059$]
questions.explanation: n=2 electrons transferred; $E^\circ=\dfrac{0.059}{n}\log K \Rightarrow 0.0295=\dfrac{0.059}{2}\log K \Rightarrow \log K=1 \Rightarrow K=10$.

questions.q: Which one of the following has a potential more than zero?
questions.explanation: For a hydrogen electrode, $E=-0.059\log[H^+]^{-1}$-type relation gives E=0 at 1M HCl (standard); at concentration greater than 1 M (2 M), the electrode potential becomes positive (greater than zero) relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.

questions.q:
$E_1$, $E_2$ and $E_3$ are the emfs of the following three galvanic cells respectively:
(i) $Zn(s)|Zn^{2+}(0.1M)||Cu^{2+}(1M)|Cu(s)$
(ii) $Zn(s)|Zn^{2+}(1M)||Cu^{2+}(1M)|Cu(s)$
(iii) $Zn(s)|Zn^{2+}(1M)||Cu^{2+}(0.1M)|Cu(s)$
Which one of the following is true?
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation $E=E^0-\dfrac{0.0591}{2}\log\dfrac{[Zn^{2+}]}{[Cu^{2+}]}$, cell (i) has the smallest ratio giving the highest emf and cell (iii) has the largest ratio giving the lowest emf, so $E_1>E_2>E_3$.

questions.q: The standard emf of a galvanic cell involving 2 moles of electrons in its redox reaction is 0.59 V. The equilibrium constant for the redox reaction of the cell is ..............

9.65 coulombs of electric current is passed through fused anhydrous $MgCl_2$. The magnesium metal thus obtained is completely converted into a Grignard reagent. The number of moles of Grignard reagent obtained is ..............
questions.explanation: Moles $e^-$=9.65/96500=$10^{-4}$; $Mg^{2+}+2e^-\to Mg$ gives moles $Mg$=$5\times10^{-5}$, which is fully converted into an equal number of moles of Grignard reagent.

questions.q: 9.65 C of electric current is passed through fused anhydrous magnesium chloride. The magnesium metal thus obtained is completely converted into a Grignard reagent. The number of moles of the Grignard reagent obtained is ...............
questions.explanation: Moles of electrons = 9.65/96500 = $10^{-4}$; Mg$^{2+}$ + 2e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Mg gives moles Mg = $5\times10^{-5}$, and Mg + RX $\rightarrow$ RMgX is 1:1, so moles Grignard reagent = $5\times10^{-5}$.

questions.q: The standard emf of a galvanic cell involving 3 moles of electrons in its redox reaction is 0.59 V. The equilibrium constant for the reaction of the cell is ...................

$E_1$, $E_2$ and $E_3$ are the emf values of the three galvanic cells respectively.

a) $Zn | Zn^{+2}_{1M} || Cu^{+2}_{0.1M} | Cu$

b) $Zn | Zn^{+2}_{1M} || Cu^{+2}_{1M} | Cu$

c) $Zn | Zn^{+2}_{0.1M} || Cu^{+2}_{1M} | Cu$

Which one of the following is true?
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation, $E=E^\circ-\dfrac{0.0591}{2}\log\dfrac{[Zn^{2+}]}{[Cu^{2+}]}$, so increasing $[Cu^{2+}]$ or decreasing $[Zn^{2+}]$ raises the emf: cell (c) (low Zn$^{2+}$, high Cu$^{2+}$) has the highest emf and cell (a) (low Cu$^{2+}$) the lowest, giving $E_3 > E_2 > E_1$.

questions.q: An aqueous solution containing 6.5 gm of NaCl of 90% purity was subjected to electrolysis. After the complete electrolysis, the solution was evaporated to get solid NaOH. The volume of 1 M acetic acid required to neutralise NaOH obtained above is
questions.explanation: Pure NaCl = 5.85 g = 0.1 mol, which on electrolysis gives 0.1 mol NaOH; volume of 1 M acetic acid needed = 0.1 mol / 1 M = 100 cm$^3$.

questions.q: The standard electrode potential for the half cell reactions are: Zn$^{++}$ + 2e$^-$ $\longrightarrow$ Zn, E° = $-0.76$ V; Fe$^{++}$ + 2e$^-$ $\longrightarrow$ Fe, E° = $-0.44$ V. The E.M.F. of the cell reaction : Fe$^{++}$ + Zn $\longrightarrow$ Zn$^{++}$ + Fe is
In the electrolysis of acidulated water, it is desired to obtain 1.12 cc of Hydrogen per second under S.T.P. condition. The current to be passed is
The one which decreases with dilution is
questions.explanation: Specific conductance decreases on dilution as ion concentration per unit volume falls, while molar/equivalent conductance increase.
